#### 1. right atrial isomerism  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.731)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:4214)

**Proposed mechanism:** GDF1 (HGNC:4214) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-176744); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-176744) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defect (HP:0001627); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-176744) —LEADS_TO→ Right atrial isomerism (MONDO:0008832). Loss-of-function mutations in GDF1 disrupt the TGF-beta signaling pathway, leading to both congenital heart defects (as seen in MONDO:0013463) and right atrial isomerism (MONDO:0008832).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in GDF1 in patients with MONDO:0013463 or right atrial isomerism would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if patients with these diseases consistently lack GDF1 variants or harbor only variants with no clear functional consequence, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs146588097)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GDF1 in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies for congenital heart defects arising from disruptions in TGF-beta signaling.

#### 6. aneurysm-osteoarthritis syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1181150)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMAD3 (HGNC:10210) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909734); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909734) —LEADS_TO→ Aortic aneurysm (HP:0002672); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909734) —LEADS_TO→ Osteoarthritis (HP:0001402); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909734) —LEADS_TO→ Thoracic aortic aneurysm (HP:0005797); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909734) —LEADS_TO→ Joint hypermobility (HP:0001252). Loss-of-function mutations in SMAD3 disrupt the TGF-beta signaling pathway, which is critical for regulating extracellular matrix production and remodeling. This disruption leads to a cascade of downstream effects, including impaired collagen synthesis and cross-linking, ultimately manifesting as aortic aneurysms (thoracic and general) and osteoarthritis, as well as joint hypermobility.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SMAD3 with a clear gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in patients with either disease would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if variants in SMAD3 are found at a high frequency (>1%) in a healthy population within gnomAD, it would suggest that SMAD3 variants alone are not sufficient to cause these specific disease phenotypes. _(variant: HGMD-CURATED:SMAD3)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SMAD3 in both conditions opens avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting the TGF-beta pathway to prevent or treat aneurysms and osteoarthritis. This could involve developing drugs that modulate SMAD3 activity or downstream effectors to restore proper extracellular matrix homeostasis.
